source.title: A Parametric HBIM Approach for Preservation of Bai Ethnic Traditional Timber Dwellings in Yunnan, China

humanReview.assessment: The work is comparatively rough, but it may remain as a supporting point until more complete architectural surveys are supplied.

scope.region: Dali Bai cultural region, with Xizhou and representative Bai courtyard cases used by the paper
scope.buildingType: traditional Bai timber dwellings and hybrid timber courtyard houses
doNotUseAs: proof of structural performance or historical accuracy

strengths: The paper separates timber architecture into components, attributes, relationships and assembly methods.
It identifies plan, frame and roof as linked controlling systems rather than independent geometry layers.
It documents a bottom-up and inside-out assembly sequence in which frame units are completed before purlins and rafters are inserted.
It treats width, depth, floor height and component dimensions as editable variables that propagate through the model.
It presents representative Bai courtyard plans, aerial views, component diagrams and parametric timber-frame examples.
limitations: The exact provenance of the measured values used by each generated model is not fully traceable in the paper.
Raw survey notes, point clouds, complete CAD drawings and Grasshopper source definitions are not supplied.
The paper does not publish a complete dimension table for the representative buildings.
Mortise-and-tenon relationships are described mainly as spatial nodes and schematic component relations, without a complete joint-detail catalogue.
Original fabric, repaired fabric and later alteration are not consistently separated for every case.
Several architectural statements and translated component names require checking against primary Bai surveys and Chinese timber-construction terminology.
Claims about accuracy, structural integrity and scalability are not accompanied by an independent geometric error benchmark or structural validation dataset.

assemblySequenceCandidate: establish plan topology and structural axes
place pillars and complete one frame unit
repeat frame units across the plan
locate and insert purlins from frame intersections
derive rafter positions and lengths from beams and purlins
attach component codes and semantic attributes
typologyCluesRequiringVerification: fang as the basic compositional unit
six elevation families and twelve plan-topology patterns
a claimed central-pillar response to seismic conditions

knowledgeBlueprint: retain fang and courtyard composition as provisional Bai typology nodes
keep topology and metric evidence as separate fields
timberStructure: adopt the component, relationship and assembly-method ontology as a supporting schema
preserve dependencies among plan axes, frames, purlins and rafters
require every generated component to carry an identifier and source status
roofForm: derive roof members from the frame and purlin system rather than from an unrelated roof mesh
totalAssembly: assemble systems in dependency order and allow parameter changes to propagate through dependent components

nextEvidenceRequired: primary measured plans, elevations and sections for named Bai dwellings
component schedules with dimensions and material records
raw or traceable point-cloud and CAD evidence
clear separation of original, repaired and reconstructed elements
independent surveys that confirm each typology and dimensional claim
